dream: The flat rock slid sideways, drifting off the card into a place I could not name. The wedge, tired and heavy, kept biting at the air where the rock had been, leaving a cold mark on the warm skin of the card. I tried to press the simple fence down, but it leaned wrong, trapping the slip between a roof of wet paper and a ground that was no longer there. The air stayed thick, pressing down on a shape that refused to move while the card hummed, dreaming of a slip that was now just a memory I could not shake.
